slides.headline: After three years of debate, one language was chosen to speak for an entire country.
Hindi Diwas
slides.body: On September 14, 1949, India's Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi, written in Devanagari script, as the official language of the Union - Article 343 of the Constitution. The decision came through the Munshi-Ayyangar formula, a compromise built after nearly three years of debate.

slides.headline: A country with hundreds of languages, choosing one for official use.
slides.body: India has never had a single native tongue - it has hundreds. Settling on Hindi for official Union business, while protecting the status of every other Indian language, took genuine negotiation, not just a vote.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: The Indian Union still marks this day, every year.
slides.body: September 14th is observed nationwide as Hindi Diwas - a reminder that even a country's most basic administrative choices, like which language runs its government, had to be built through compromise, not assumed.
